messages:
Liam (sales_eng): FYI AcmeOps POC: they can see requests in Redwood console but Datadog traces aren't linking. logs show a trace header key but Datadog isn't matching. also experiencing intermittent 429s during load test.
Priya (solutions): can you paste a sample log line + headers from their app? also which drain/export are they using (datadog-forwarder-v2 or legacy)?
Jordan (acmeops): sample log + headers below. we're using datadog-forwarder-v2 from the Console.

LOG: 2026-03-21T09:12:03Z INFO req incoming path=/v1/chat status=200 latency_ms=63 trace_header=00-7f9c2e1a...-0000000000000001-01 request_id=""
HEADERS: Authorization=Bearer ***, Content-Type=application/json, X-Forwarded-For=10.0.0.1

Jordan (acmeops): note trace_header shows up as a single string in our app logs but the field name isn't trace_id and Datadog doesn't pick it up.
Ravi (obs-eng): two problems: 1) header name must be traceparent (W3C) or we must map the header into the JSON field trace_id in the drain. 2) seems like your LB or ingress may be overwriting/stripping traceparent -> confirm.
Ravi (obs-eng): quick actions: a) send a test curl with traceparent and check response x-redwood-trace header, b) update log shipper to emit trace_id: <hex> c) add backoff for 429s or request temporary burst.
Priya (solutions): Jordan, try this curl and paste response headers: 

curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -H 'traceparent: 00-7f9c2e1a4b34d6f9c3a1b2e3d4f5678-abcdef1234567890-01' \n  -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'

Jordan (acmeops): response headers: x-redwood-trace=7f9c2e1a4b34d6f9c3a1b2e3d4f5678, content-type=application/json
Jordan (acmeops): updated log sample after sending traceparent:

2026-03-21T09:18:10Z INFO req incoming path=/v1/chat status=200 latency_ms=45 trace_id=7f9c2e1a4b34d6f9c3a1b2e3d4f5678 request_id=req-42

Ravi (obs-eng): good — that proves propagation works when the client sends traceparent. Next: update your app to set traceparent on outbound calls to Redwood. Example (node fetch): 

await fetch(url, { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${KEY}`, 'traceparent': tp }, body: JSON.stringify(body) })

Ravi (obs-eng): For Datadog linking, the drain must emit a field named "trace_id" (hex trace id) or Datadog will not autocorrelate. If your shipper only writes trace_header, add a pipeline rule to copy trace_header -> trace_id and ensure the value is the 32 hex chars.
Liam (sales_eng): any short-term fix for the 429s? demo tomorrow.
Ravi (obs-eng): short-term: exponential backoff + jitter and reduce concurrency. I can also open a temporary burst allocation for the POC project. longer term: reserve a small dedicated pool for predictable throughput.
observability-bot: Export updated: datadog-forwarder-v2-acme (ndjson) 2026-03-21T09:22:01Z
Priya (solutions): Ravi, can you create the burst request?
Ravi (obs-eng): opened ticket INC-8621 to allow a temporary burst for project acme-poc until 2026-03-24. added checklist: how to detect header stripping (search logs for missing x-redwood-trace), sample mapping for Datadog, and backoff snippet.
Jordan (acmeops): applied mapping in our logshipper to copy trace_header -> trace_id and validated in Datadog: I can now search for trace_id:7f9c2e1a4b34d6f9c3a1b2e3d4f5678 and see spans + logs linked. 429s reduced after throttling; demo looks stable.
Liam (sales_eng): awesome — thanks everyone. marking resolved unless anything else crops up.
Priya (solutions): I'll follow up with a quick runbook for AcmeOps with the curl snippet and mapping steps.
Ravi (obs-eng): happy to pair on their CI env if needed.
